FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:29 AM
FHLBank Chicago: $62 Million Affordable Housing Grants To Support 1,786 Homes Across Illinois And Wisconsin
The Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago has awarded $62 million through its 2026 Affordable Housing Program General Fund to finance 47 affordable housing projects in Illinois and Wisconsin. The funding will support the acquisition, rehabilitation, and construction of 1,786 affordable housing units across the two states.
The awards include an additional $10 million approved by FHLBank Chicago’s Board of Directors to expand support for affordable housing development.
The grants are intended to address housing affordability challenges as development costs and constrained housing supply continue to affect communities.
FHLBank Chicago operates as a regional member-owned cooperative within the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
Its member institutions include commercial banks, credit unions, insurance companies, savings institutions, and community development financial institutions.
The Affordable Housing Program provides grants to support projects sponsored through participating member institutions.
Applications are submitted by housing developers, government organizations, public housing authorities, tribally designated organizations, and other eligible participants.
The funding helps bridge gaps between the cost of providing affordable housing and the financing available through other sources.
The 2026 awards cover projects involving different housing needs and development approaches.
One recipient is Reclaiming Chicago NFP, which received support for the construction of 24 affordable single-family homes on vacant city-owned lots.
The homes will be developed across four Chicago neighborhoods: Back of the Yards, Roseland, North Lawndale, and Washington Park.
The project is sponsored by First Eagle Bank, a member of FHLBank Chicago.
It is part of an initiative organized by United Power for Action and Justice, a coalition that brings together civic and religious organizations.
Five nonprofit development partners are participating in the effort.
The project is intended to expand opportunities for homeownership while returning vacant properties to productive residential use.
First Eagle Bank has also provided a $1 million interest-free loan to support the development.
The combination of financing and grant support is intended to help move the project toward construction.
Another award will support Milwaukee Development Corporation’s conversion of a former hospital into affordable apartments.
The project will create 124 residences for adults ages 55 and older.
Of those units, 25 will be designated as supportive housing for residents with disabilities.
Jewish Family Services will provide on-site services to eligible residents.
Associated Bank is sponsoring the project through the Affordable Housing Program.
The redevelopment is intended to preserve a historic building while introducing additional affordable housing options for older adults.
Projects like these illustrate the program’s support for both new construction and the reuse of existing properties.
Since the Affordable Housing Program General Fund began in 1989, FHLBank Chicago has allocated more than $630 million in grants through the end of 2025.
These investments have helped provide housing for more than 85,000 households.
The latest $62 million allocation represents another significant commitment to affordable housing development across the bank’s two-state district.
The organization believes the funding will help developers and community partners move projects forward despite rising construction costs and financing challenges.
By supporting 47 projects and 1,786 housing units, FHLBank Chicago aims to expand access to affordable homes while strengthening neighborhoods across Illinois and Wisconsin.
KEY QUOTES:
“Affordable housing remains a pressing need across Illinois and Wisconsin, as rising development costs and limited housing supply continue to challenge communities. By increasing our investment in this year’s AHP General Fund, we’re able to support more affordable housing and help our members and community organizations move critical projects forward.”
Michael Ericson, President And CEO Of FHLBank Chicago
“FHLBank Chicago’s Affordable Housing Program plays an important role in closing financing gaps and making affordable housing projects possible. We’re proud to support Reclaiming Chicago’s efforts to transform vacant lots into affordable homes and create meaningful homeownership opportunities for Chicago families. Beyond sponsoring the AHP grant, First Eagle Bank has also provided a $1 million interest-free loan to help advance this important initiative. We strongly believe in Reclaiming Chicago’s mission, and their efforts to revitalize neighborhoods and expand affordable homeownership have certainly not gone unnoticed.”
Faruk Daudbasic, Senior Vice President Of Commercial Lending And Community Development At First Eagle Bank
“This development will bring much-needed affordable housing to Milwaukee while preserving an important part of the neighborhood’s history. We’re grateful to FHLBank Chicago and Associated Bank for supporting a project that will help older adults live independently with access to the services they need.”
Pat O’Brien, President Of Milwaukee Development Corporation

Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:19 AM
Oyster Therapeutics: $60 Million Series A-2 Funding To Advance Alzheimer’s Drug Development And Protein Degradation Platform
Oyster Therapeutics, formerly known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, has raised $60 million in Series A-2 funding to advance its next-generation targeted protein degradation technology for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. The financing will support the development of the company’s lead oral tau degrader toward clinical trials while expanding its proprietary SELFTAC drug discovery platform. The round was led by 4BIO Capital, a London-based venture capital firm specializing in life sciences, with participation from new investors Eli Lilly and Company, CE Ventures, Actium Group, and TOHO Ventures, which is managed by Global Brain.
Existing investors Syncona, Oxford Science Enterprises, Mission BioCapital, and MGB Ventures also participated.
The financing comes as the company rebrands from Kesmalea Therapeutics to Oyster Therapeutics, reflecting its transition toward clinical development and broader ambitions in neuroscience.
Headquartered in London, Oyster is developing medicines based on targeted protein degradation, a therapeutic approach designed to eliminate disease-associated proteins by using the body’s natural cellular protein disposal mechanisms.
Unlike conventional treatments that may inhibit the activity of particular proteins, targeted protein degraders are designed to trigger their removal from cells.
Oyster is initially focusing on neurodegenerative diseases involving abnormal accumulations of the tau protein.
Tau plays an important role in maintaining healthy neuronal structures, but abnormal forms can accumulate and contribute to diseases known as tauopathies.
Alzheimer’s disease is among the best-known conditions associated with pathological tau accumulation.
The company’s lead program is an orally administered, brain-penetrant tau degrader designed to selectively remove harmful forms of tau while preserving healthy tau.
Developing medicines capable of reaching the central nervous system presents considerable challenges because the blood-brain barrier restricts the passage of many therapeutic compounds.
Traditional bifunctional protein degraders can be relatively large molecules, limiting their ability to cross biological membranes and reach brain tissue.
Oyster’s proprietary SELFTAC platform is designed to address this limitation by enabling larger targeted protein degraders to function as smaller molecular components.
The technology uses a reversible linker connecting two molecular structures, commonly called warheads.
One component binds to the targeted protein, while the other recruits the cellular machinery responsible for protein degradation.
The reversible linker enables the components to exist as smaller molecules that can more readily penetrate biological membranes.
The molecules are subsequently designed to self-assemble into a functional bifunctional degrader capable of triggering the removal of the intended protein.
Oyster believes this approach could improve central nervous system penetration while preserving the versatility of conventional targeted protein degradation technology.
The company also expects its smaller molecular designs to support oral administration, potentially making treatments more convenient for patients.
Oral therapies can offer practical advantages for diseases affecting large populations, including simplified administration, room-temperature storage, and potentially lower manufacturing costs.
Beyond its lead tau program, Oyster intends to use SELFTAC as a platform for generating additional targeted protein degrader candidates.
The technology incorporates a modular design that supports high-throughput screening of different molecular combinations.
This approach is intended to accelerate candidate identification while improving the efficiency of drug discovery.
Oyster has also established a sponsored research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to strengthen its tau biology research capabilities.
The collaboration will provide access to patient-derived neuronal cell lines and specialized methods for generating and detecting oligomeric tau.
Oligomeric tau refers to aggregated forms of the protein that are considered particularly relevant to neurodegenerative disease processes.
The research will be supervised by Dr. Catarina Silva, an investigator at the Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute and Assistant Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School.
The collaboration is intended to help Oyster evaluate its therapeutic candidates in biologically relevant systems and strengthen its understanding of disease-associated tau.
The $60 million financing will support continued preclinical development, advancement toward human studies, and further investment in the SELFTAC platform.
Oyster’s strategy reflects increasing interest in therapeutic approaches that directly address proteins implicated in neurodegenerative conditions.
However, the company’s lead program remains investigational, and its safety and effectiveness in patients have not yet been established.
As Oyster advances toward clinical development, the company will seek to demonstrate whether its technology can effectively reach the brain and selectively degrade disease-associated proteins.
The rebranding marks a new phase for the business as it works to translate its protein degradation research into potential treatments for Alzheimer’s and other neurological diseases.

Index Industries will launch the USHP Index, a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices, made investable through USHP, a liquid index product, issued by USHP Limited.
NEW YORK , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Index Industries emerges from stealth with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures, Wintermute Ventures, and other institutional investors. The company is building the technology and infrastructure to transform U.S. housing into a broadly investable asset class. Its platform combines a daily-reporting index with tokenization technology and real estate and capital markets services to power third-party housing-linked investment products. USHP , based on Index Industries' U.S. Home Price Index and issued by USHP Limited (BVI), will be the first investment product built on the platform.
U.S. housing is a $55 trillion market, making it one of the largest asset classes in the U.S. Yet despite its scale, broad-based investment exposure to U.S. home prices has remained difficult to access through traditional financial products. Index Industries was founded to close that gap.
Index Industries' first offering will be the U.S. Home Price Index (USHP Index), a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices. Calculated daily, it integrates data from the major housing indices into a single national measure, providing a continuous and comprehensive read on home prices. The index is intended to support housing-market research, reporting, and portfolio monitoring and housing-related financial products.
Index Industries is co-founded by Josh Rosenthal, who joins as CEO following his role as President and General Partner of Polychain Capital, and Brian Hardecker, a former Principal at Blackstone and the Founder and CEO of Longmark, a leading residential real estate platform formed in 2021 that has $2 billion in assets under management. Index Industries combines two worlds of expertise to bring breakthrough tokenization technology to new real estate assets.
"Indexing is one of the most important and least celebrated innovations in modern finance. It reduces the expertise and cost barriers to investing in an entire market, which is what U.S. housing needs," said Josh Rosenthal, co-founder & CEO of Index Industries. "I've spent my career looking for industry-shaping financial technology, and Index Industries is exactly that. It has the potential to change how the world sees housing: not just as a roof over your head or something that is out of reach, but as an investable asset class."

Mosaic Raises $47M Seed to Develop Spatial Intelligence for Surgery
Published

By
Nova Jain, AI Entrepreneurship & Founders AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Mosaic Intelligence Labs announced on November 10, 2026 that it had emerged from stealth with $47 million in seed funding to develop sensing-enabled spatial intelligence and robotic systems for surgery, initially focusing on procedures performed through the vascular system.
The San Francisco company named 8VC, Fundomo, Lingotto Innovation and Obvious Ventures among its backers. Chief executive Ileana Pirozzi and chief technology officer Alison “Ali” Kight Mackanic founded Mosaic after meeting during their doctoral studies at Stanford. Their work alongside clinicians exposed how difficult, less-invasive procedures often remain tied to knowledge held by individual operators.
“We kept returning to one question: what would it take to scale the knowledge of the very best surgeons?” Pirozzi said. “We believe that starts with making our machines aware, and turning surgical repetition into experience we can learn from.”
Starting With Endovascular Procedures
Mosaic’s initial target is endovascular care. In these procedures, physicians thread flexible wires and catheters through blood vessels to reach treatment sites. Mosaic describes blood vessels as routes to virtually every organ, yet operators have no direct line of sight inside them. They use live X-ray imaging, preoperative scans and the feel of the instruments to work out where they are and what lies ahead.
The company identifies radiation exposure and outcomes that vary with operator experience as limitations of that workflow. Interpreting the available signals can take years of practice, and much of the resulting knowledge is difficult to record or hand down. The result is a mismatch: surgical access has become less invasive, while navigation still depends heavily on the perception and judgment of the person holding the instrument.
For context, Mosaic’s website compares open surgery’s 20–30 cm incision and keyhole surgery’s 1–2 cm ports with endovascular surgery’s 2 mm needle puncture, and lists stopping strokes, clearing blocked coronary arteries, repairing aneurysms and restoring blood flow to limbs among current applications. That range helps explain why Mosaic is treating vascular navigation as a reusable capability across multiple procedures.
Giving Surgical Instruments a Learning Loop
The technical design begins by instrumenting the point where surgical tools meet anatomy. Mosaic intends to combine those sensor readings with computation that reconstructs the vascular environment from within, maintaining a three-dimensional picture of anatomy and instrument position as it changes. A robotic interface would support precise instrument control.
The learning architecture would record the environment, instrument movement and physician actions as synchronized streams. Physical models would then help the system relate what it senses to what happens when it moves. The release connects this approach to the robotics concept of a world model: a representation of an environment that helps a machine predict how its actions will change that environment.
All of these capabilities remain development goals; the announcement supplies no patient-outcome findings or clinical-performance results. The nearer objective is to assist physicians’ perception and control, while the recorded procedures are intended to become a source of cumulative learning for machines over time.
Recruiting and Longer-Term Treatment Goals
Mosaic is recruiting engineers, physicians and creatives in San Francisco. Open roles cover hardware engineering, sensing, perception, machine learning and clinical engineering, matching a technical effort that spans physical instruments, software, robotics and clinical practice.
Mosaic’s longer-term goal is to widen the treatments delivered through these vascular routes. The company says catheters can deliver drugs, energy, biologics and other therapies directly to a target site, and that more reliable navigation could expand both the range of treatments delivered through blood vessels and the settings in which clinicians can offer them.
Mosaic’s near-term product challenge and longer-term data ambition are linked: dependable navigation must work in individual procedures before those procedures can provide a useful foundation for cumulative machine learning.

Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
By Amit Chowdhry

Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
Coframe, an artificial intelligence company developing self-optimizing digital experiences, has raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A round co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital. The investment will support development of the company’s autonomous AI platform, which continuously generates, tests, and improves websites, landing pages, and advertising campaigns. The financing also included participation from executives and technology leaders associated with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.
Coframe is developing what founder and CEO Josh Payne describes as the “living internet,” a model in which websites and other digital interfaces adapt continuously based on user interactions and business objectives.
Traditional websites generally display predetermined content and require development teams to make changes through scheduled design, engineering, and marketing projects.
Coframe’s platform is designed to automate much of that process by generating new content and design variations, testing their performance, and deploying improvements.
The company uses a specialized transformer model trained on user behavior alongside a team of AI agents responsible for different aspects of the optimization process.
Those agents perform functions resembling a strategist, designer, software engineer, quality assurance specialist, and data scientist.
Together, they can generate and evaluate hundreds of website or advertising variations within minutes.
The technology analyzes how visitors interact with digital experiences and uses those results to improve future versions.
Coframe says the platform can personalize content for different visitors while continuously adjusting interfaces to support conversion and engagement objectives.
The company reports that its technology has generated more than $300 million in incremental revenue for customers.
Its customer base includes Dropbox, Boston Consulting Group, Block, Backcountry, Sur La Table, and other businesses.
According to Coframe, customers have experienced conversion rate increases of 158% at Dropbox, 410% at Replit, and 60% at Cash App.
The company also reported that a Fortune 500 customer achieved a 70% increase in conversion within 30 days of signing its contract.
Across its customer base, Coframe says conversion rates have improved by more than 20% on average.
These performance figures are company-reported results and may vary across different implementations and customer environments.
At Dropbox, Coframe said an experiment that previously required approximately four weeks of engineering, design, and quality assurance work was created and deployed in 30 minutes.
The platform has also reported a 39% experiment success rate across thousands of tested variations.
Coframe says this represents more than three times the industry average, while customers have increased their experimentation frequency by tenfold or more.
Beyond website and advertising optimization, Coframe is developing capabilities for applications, email, and other digital experiences.
The company is also preparing for an internet in which AI agents increasingly perform research, product comparisons, and purchases on behalf of users.
Coframe announced a collaboration with OpenAI involving its ChatGPT advertising offering.
The collaboration is intended to help customers optimize advertisements and landing pages as a connected experience.
It builds on an earlier partnership focused on training a specialized model to generate brand-aligned code and creative assets.
Coframe is also incorporating AI agent considerations into the websites it builds.
Payne founded Coframe in 2023 after studying Mathematics and Computer Science at Stanford University.
He previously co-founded Autograph with Tom Brady, a business that reached a valuation exceeding $2 billion.
Payne also developed GPT-Migrate, an early autonomous coding agent.
Coframe has expanded its leadership through acquisitions of companies founded by two former Optimizely executives.
Bo Mohazzabi now serves as Vice President of Go-to-Market, while Steven Ebin is General Manager of Revenue Optimization.
The new financing will support Coframe’s efforts to develop more sophisticated AI systems for digital experience creation and optimization.
By combining autonomous software development, design, analytics, and personalization, Coframe aims to reduce the time required to improve digital experiences while helping businesses increase conversion rates and revenue.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re building an internet that improves itself. A digital experience should understand what it is trying to accomplish, adapt to the person interacting with it and learn from every result. Instead of waiting months for the next redesign, companies should have websites and applications that get better every day.”
Josh Payne, Founder And CEO Of Coframe
“For decades, the web has been frozen in place, showing every visitor essentially the same page. Coframe is building the living internet, where two people can visit the same website and have completely different experiences, personalized to who they are and what they need. These interfaces continuously learn and improve themselves. This is a huge leap beyond traditional A/B testing and the next iteration of the internet.”
Vinod Khosla, Founder Of Khosla Ventures
“The way most companies build and manage their user interfaces today is wrong, and in a year or two it will be obvious why that is. User interfaces should improve themselves, and be personalized to every user.”
Pavlo Razumovskyi, Co-Founder And Vice President Of Engineering At Coframe

NEW YORK , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nidus, the robotics company deploying embodied intelligence inside America's defense factories, announced $30 million in funding today, backed by Kleiner Perkins and Costanoa, with participation from Ludlow Ventures, SF1, Absolute Partners, Tau, and angel investors, including Chris Power, founder of Hadrian; Adrian Aoun, co-founder of Dulo, Foundational Industries and Seneca; and Nikhil Goel, Chief Commercial Officer at Archer.
America's defense industrial base has a capacity crisis. The country that once produced more than half the world's goods now relies heavily on overseas supply chains to manufacture parts for its own weapons systems. This constitutes a national security risk, and factories urgently need to increase output to meet demand.
Nidus builds embodied intelligence that lets traditional industrial robots perform precision assembly tasks. The company develops and deploys foundation robotics models across America's critical defense factories, using sovereign AI training practices. This lets each customer retain its collective knowledge, which is crucial in secure environments.
"I grew up in rural South Carolina and watched offshoring create the current industrial base crisis," said Justin Sealy, co-founder and CEO of Nidus. "At this point, we can't out-labor or out-scale our competition. We need to leapfrog the rest of the world by deploying physical AI that scales America's existing industrial capacity. This is why we started Nidus."
Nidus is deploying across the defense industrial base and quickly eclipsed seven figures in revenue in its first four months. The company is currently delivering customized models to automate wire processing on its proprietary platform, which was built from the ground up to meet Department of War security requirements.
"In physical AI, the value will accrue to players that prioritize deployment and customer value. And Nidus is the rare team that has actually deployed AI into the most locked-down environments in the country" said Aatish Nayak, partner at Kleiner Perkins. It is currently occupied by a vacant nine-story parking garage.
Pro-H Group plans to demolish the existing structure and develop a residential property containing a mixture of one- to four-bedroom condominium homes.
The proposed building will also include resident amenities.
The project is located near Union Square, an established neighborhood known for transportation connections, retail businesses, restaurants, and residential demand.

Finite State has raised $27 million in Series C funding to expand its AI-driven product security platform and international operations. The round was led by private funds managed by The O.H.I.O. Fund , with participation from CIBC Innovation Banking , Energy Impact Partners , Energize Capital , and National Grid Partners .
The Columbus, Ohio-based company focuses on a problem that becomes more consequential as vulnerability discovery accelerates: manufacturers need to know what software actually runs inside the devices they sell. A flaw in a shared component can affect vehicles, medical equipment, industrial systems, or consumer electronics, but determining which finished products contain that component can be difficult.
Finite State plans to use the capital to deepen its presence in international markets and develop more autonomous platform capabilities. Its technology combines analysis of software artifacts with vulnerability intelligence and compliance workflows, aiming to turn an inventory of shipped code into decisions about what needs attention.
Inspecting the Software That Actually Ships
Connected products are assembled from many sources: an operating system, open-source libraries, supplier SDKs, board-support packages, and proprietary applications. Manufacturers may control their own source code while having limited visibility into compiled components supplied by other vendors.
A build manifest describes what a development process expects to include. Firmware analysis examines the artifact produced by that process. The difference matters when packaging adds a component, a supplier modifies a library, or a dependency is compiled directly into an executable.
Finite State’s binary-analysis documentation describes unpacking firmware images, containers, archives, and executables, then identifying components through binary software composition analysis. It also applies static application security testing to compiled code, examining weaknesses beyond a simple list of package names.
The resulting inventory can include modified and statically linked components, with findings enriched by vulnerability, exploit, and license information. The analysis also looks for hard-coded credentials, exposed keys, and cryptographic issues. Supported inputs include firmware, shared libraries, mobile application binaries, and third-party software, as well as source code when available.
This is the foundation of the company’s pitch: security decisions should follow the contents of the finished product, rather than depend entirely on the documentation that accompanies it.
Turning a Component Inventory Into a Remediation Decision
Finding a vulnerable component is only the beginning. A product team still needs to determine whether the affected code can be reached, whether an exploit is relevant to the device’s configuration, and which releases or product variants need a fix.
Finite State’s platform overview describes prioritization based on reachability, exploit intelligence, and product context. The aim is to reduce the time engineers spend investigating findings that do not represent the same level of practical exposure.
A software bill of materials, or SBOM, records the components in a product. Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange, or VEX, adds information about whether a particular vulnerability affects that product. Together, those records help distinguish an inventory question—whether a component is present—from an assessment of the risk it creates.
Finite State says its platform can identify known and previously unknown vulnerabilities. That combines different kinds of analysis: matching components against disclosed issues and examining compiled code for weaknesses. The usefulness of the result depends on the evidence behind a finding and its relevance to the device, not simply the number of alerts produced.
AI Automation Still Needs Evidence About Analysis Quality
One practical example of the company’s AI work is its AI Unpacking Evaluation Agent , introduced earlier in 2026. The agent evaluates how completely an uploaded artifact was extracted and explains gaps that may limit the subsequent analysis.
That step is important because a scan cannot assess code it never successfully extracted. Encrypted containers, nested archives, or unusual firmware packaging can leave part of an artifact outside the scanner’s view.
Finite State says the agent supplies a quality rating, identifies likely causes of incomplete extraction, and recommends actions such as decrypting content, unpacking it locally, or repackaging an archive before another upload. The automation helps teams understand what the analysis covered, rather than treating every completed scan as equally comprehensive.
The broader platform connects that analysis to reviewable workflows. Its published architecture describes bringing firmware, binaries, source code, supplier SBOMs, and documentation into a common process for generating security findings, verification evidence, and reports.
Connecting Product Security to Compliance Work
The financing announcement places regulatory pressure alongside faster vulnerability discovery as a driver of demand. Manufacturers increasingly need evidence showing how they identified software risks, assessed their impact, and addressed them across the product lifecycle.
Finite State generates SBOMs, VEX records, and compliance packages tied to product artifacts. Its platform also links architecture, security requirements, and verification work, helping teams connect a design decision with the software that reaches a customer.

Productivity gurus online these days say AI agents should book your travel, manage calendars, and send emails. Lumbra thinks they can do a whole lot more, and so far, a rapidly growing list of customers in the intelligence community and the Pentagon agree. Investors do too.
This morning, the DC-based AI startup announced a $25M Series A to keep scaling its AI agent operating system and agent harness across the defense and national security space and expand into “regulated commercial sectors,” the company told Tectonic exclusively.
Point 72 Ventures and Ansa Capital co-led the round, with participation from the company’s OG backer, Costanoa Ventures.
Secret agent: Founded by ex-Army Ranger and CIA counterterrorism officer Aaron Brown (CEO) and fellow Ranger—and MIT-trained computer scientist—Michael Hiebert (CTO), Lumbra’s pitch is that AI agents have the potential to be incredibly capable tools for analysts and decision-makers in national security, but they need the right operating framework, or harness, to make their analysis work auditable, verifiable, and trustworthy.
Lumbra’s platform, called LumbraOS, does that with three core offerings:
Nebula is the agent orchestrator that records actions, traces claims to sources, and enforces data protection. The human running the agents fact-checks those findings and analysis workflows before they’re relayed to a system of record.
StarChart is a customer organization’s knowledge graph where agents automatically compound knowledge as they work, with “insights and conclusions recorded alongside sources and sensitivity labels,” according to Lumbra.
Astrolabe is the agent evaluator that tests them before deployment and tracks scores in production using the customer’s benchmarks.
Put simply, “We’re building a coordination layer for intelligence advantage and decision intelligence—it’s the harness, it’s the control panel, the control layer, it’s the consumption layer,” Brown told Tectonic . “We’re putting the controls in place, the data lineage, the explainability, the coordination layer, the benchmark, and the evaluations, plus the harness.”
The platform is “model-neutral” (as opposed to model-agnostic), meaning it can run a range of frontier and open-source models depending on the performance level required for the task agents are running.
“To do some of these tasks, there’s a level of ability that the model has to be above,” Brown said. “It just needs to be a model that is at that level of performance, so we’re model neutral with strong model opinions.”
Rolling out: So far, that’s proven to be a hit with intelligence community customers—where Lumbra signed its first contracts—and increasingly with a self-proclaimed “AI-first” Defense Department. Lumbra is already under contract, with its agents in production on top-secret networks across the Pentagon and IC.
Lumbra was one of two companies—the other being a small company you might’ve heard of called Palantir— tapped by the Pentagon’s Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO) for the “Agent Network” Pace-Setting Project under the Department’s AI Acceleration Strategy.
Under that contract, Lumbra is responsible for implementing “AI orchestration technology operational on US Government systems” to “compress the time it takes to turn intelligence into informed options for commanders around the world.”
The trust element is a big reason for Lumbra’s hot start with defense customers and on classified networks.
“There are a lot of different ways you can slice up these potential agentic systems. For us, especially when it’s leading to a consequential decision, everything needs the ability to be explained,” Brown said. “You need to be able to allow a human, who’s cognitively limited compared to these machines, to be able to consume that quickly and say, ‘All right, now I trust this output because I read it with my own eyes.’”
That said, Brown doesn’t think agents are ready to take over all elements of the intelligence analysis workflow—especially targeting decisions.
“I say over and over again, these systems are nowhere near ready enough to do any type of automated targeting work—I wouldn’t trust it; nobody should trust it,” he said. “What they can do, which is spectacular, is help humans know much more about a target than they would ever be able to know on their own.”
Growing up and out: With a fresh $25M in the bank, Lumbra is looking to take that validation earned in the most high-consequence environments into the commercial world, especially in highly regulated sectors. According to Brown, the company is already “working with some private companies in a B2B relationship—some very big ones.”
For a startup that itself is “agent-pilled,” as Brown put it, he’s betting that Lumbra will be “one of the first examples of a 100-200 person company that swings like a 2,000-3,000 person company,” he said. “I don’t think anyone who’s touching our product right now would say anything other than we’re at the front edge of this compared to anyone else in the game.”

AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital joining existing lead investors Samsara BioCapital and Lightstone Ventures
Financing supports TNFα development candidate nomination and initiation of IND-enabling studies, alongside advancement of oral TL1A inhibitors into lead optimization
Proprietary QUAISAR platform, combined with approach to Physical AI, continues to drive rapid design of optimized oral drug candidates
WATERTOWN, Mass., Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PsiThera, a biotechnology company harnessing biologically relevant protein states and physical artificial intelligence to create oral drugs for immune and inflammatory diseases, today announced the closing of a $25 million financing. New investors AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital participated, along with existing lead investors Samsara BioCapital and Lightstone Ventures, and other existing investors. In connection with the financing, Claire Leurent, Ph.D., MBA, Managing Director at AbbVie Ventures, has joined PsiThera’s Board of Directors.
Proceeds from the financing are expected to fund operations, supporting development candidate nomination and the initiation of IND-enabling studies for the company’s lead oral small molecule TNFα inhibitor, as well as advancement of its oral TL1A program into lead optimization.
The company’s proprietary QUAISAR platform combines physics-based molecular simulation, machine learning, and experimental biophysics into a single closed-loop discovery engine to design novel small molecule therapeutics more efficiently. QUAISAR models protein motion to identify and target transient binding pockets that conventional structure-based design cannot see, enabling the design of small molecules for targets that have been difficult to address with oral therapies. Using this platform, PsiThera advanced the company’s lead TNFα program from hit identification to lead optimization in just four months.
“Our goal is to bring the efficacy of leading biologics into novel oral medicines to improve on their therapeutic profiles. This financing accelerates our progress toward that vision as we advance our oral TNFα program toward development candidate nomination and clinical initiation and expand our pipeline of differentiated immunology therapeutics, starting with TL1A,” said Eric D. Shaff, President and Chief Executive Officer of PsiThera. “We are grateful for the continued support of our existing investors and welcome AbbVie Ventures and Lumination Capital.”
Injectable anti-TNFα biologic therapies are approved across a broad range of immune-mediated diseases. However, an oral therapeutic could have broad application, both as monotherapy and as a combination partner, and provide an additional treatment option to the many patients who have not yet started biologic therapy.
PsiThera’s oral TNFα inhibitors are designed to achieve a differentiated profile to improve the therapeutic index relative to injectables or other oral TNFα inhibitors in development, supporting best-in-class potential.
“PsiThera has brought together seasoned biopharma leadership, experienced drug hunters, and immunology and computational scientists around a platform that can find and exploit protein states that conventional approaches cannot effectively drug,” said Christina Isacson, Ph.D., Chair of PsiThera’s Board of Directors and Partner at Lightstone Ventures. “Our progress with TNFα and TL1A is illustrative of the power of the platform. With this financing, the Company is well-positioned to advance its lead programs and extend its platform across a broader immunology pipeline.”
About PsiThera
PsiThera is a biotechnology company harnessing biologically relevant protein states and physical artificial intelligence to create oral drugs for immune and inflammatory diseases, therapeutic areas historically reliant on injectables. By integrating biophysics, computational modeling, and mechanistic biology through its QUAISAR platform, PsiThera’s expert drug hunters discover new therapeutic opportunities and optimized drugs. The company’s initial programs target clinically validated cytokine pathways, including TNFα, TL1A, and IL-6. PsiThera is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts. CAMBRIDGE, Mass. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nanopath , a point-of-care diagnostics company enabling laboratory-quality molecular testing in minutes, today announced the close of a $25 million Series B financing round, which includes $2 million in non-dilutive grant financing. The round is co-led by Norwest and SV Health Investors' MedTech Convergence Fund, alongside strategic participation from the Labcorp Venture Fund. New and existing investors also participated, including Elderberry Ventures, GingerBread Capital, and Alumni Ventures.
As part of the financing, Catherine Kiani, J.D., Managing Partner at Elderberry Ventures, and Mindy Nye, Ph.D., Vice President, Labcorp Diagnostics, have joined the Nanopath Board as Observers.
"Nanopath is developing truly transformative technology with the potential to reshape the molecular diagnostics industry and dramatically improve patient outcomes," said Jeff Crowe, Senior Managing Partner at Norwest. "We are beyond excited to continue supporting the company at this key inflection point."
Nanopath has developed the first clinical diagnostics platform built on plasmonic biosensing. The company's proprietary optical biosensing technology is designed to enable molecular detection without nucleic acid amplification, a step required by PCR-based tests. "We've spent years developing and pressure-testing a fundamentally new approach to molecular diagnostics for patients who have been overlooked for far too long," said Alison Burklund, Ph.D., Co-Founder & Co-CEO of Nanopath. "This funding brings us closer to the next and most important step – translating that innovation into meaningful clinical impact."
The funding will support key milestones toward the potential commercial launch of Nanopath's 15-minute point-of-care vaginitis assay, including manufacturing scale-up and initiation of Nanopath's Food and Drug Administration 510(k) clinical study. Nanopath will also use the funding to expand its team across clinical and commercial functions as it prepares for launch. "We're incredibly proud of the extraordinary team we've built at Nanopath and our shared commitment to transforming women's healthcare," said Amogha Tadimety, Ph.D., Co-Founder & Co-CEO of Nanopath. "We're grateful for the confidence of our investors and excited to build on this momentum as we enter our next phase of growth."
By delivering accurate results during a single visit, Nanopath aims to establish a new standard of care for women's health and expand access to high-quality diagnostics for women across the United States. Over time, the platform is expected to expand to other clinical indications, improving healthcare by making sophisticated diagnostics more accessible at the point of care.
The vaginitis test is currently under development and has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Commercial availability is subject to successful completion of development activities and applicable regulatory review.
About Nanopath
Nanopath is a women-led company dedicated to improving health equity worldwide, starting with women's health. Nanopath's proprietary molecular diagnostic testing platform takes a radically new approach to how clinicians characterize human health. The company's novel biosensing technology has the potential to enable fast, high-complexity testing at the point-of-care, rather than in centralized laboratories. The company is headquartered in Cambridge, Mass., at The Engine built by MIT, a premier facility for high-potential, tough-tech start-ups. Founded in 2020, Nanopath has raised more than $46 million, and is backed by Norwest, the Medtech Convergence Fund, an SV Health Investors Fund, Elderberry Ventures, GingerBread Capital, Alumni Ventures and the Labcorp Venture Fund. SPARETECH aims to cut manufacturers' spare parts inventory by 60% within three years with AI that ensures parts are available when they are needed
MUNICH , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SPARETECH, a provider of enterprise AI for spare parts management, today announced it has raised $20 million in Series B funding to help manufacturers cut their spare parts inventory without risking downtime. Blume Equity and Insight Partners co-led the round, with participation from Headline.
Geographic expansion and growth trajectory
Continue Reading
SPARETECH Founders | Dr. Lukas Biedermann & Martin Weber
SPARETECH has established itself in the United States and grown its revenue fivefold since the start of 2024. Over the same period, the company grew its spare parts catalog to more than 40 million verified parts and expanded its network to 15,000 manufacturer and supplier partners. The global rollout of Nestlé, a SPARETECH customer, put 320 plants across 70 countries live in less than a year, further affirming SPARETECH's global enterprise capabilities and speed.
"Every customer we work with wants the same thing: the production line running with less inventory on the shelf. That is the problem we are going to solve with Maintenance teams, and our goal is to cut spare parts inventory by 60% in the next three years, while securing the same uptime."
Martin Weber, CEO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why spare parts stay on the shelf
Spare parts management has long been one of manufacturing's most persistent inefficiencies. A single stockout can halt production and idle an entire line, making plants default to holding extensive spare parts inventories as a safeguard. The result is a substantial amount of capital sitting on the shelf. SPARETECH's 2026 benchmark report puts the average value of spare parts inventory at $169 million per company.
Source: Unlocking cost savings in spare parts management: The 2026 benchmark report on MRO spend, productivity, and working capital , SPARETECH, 2026.
From visibility to availability
Since its founding, SPARETECH has helped customers gain visibility into the parts they hold and standardize their spare parts data, which is the foundation of effective spare parts management. Meaningfully reducing inventory levels, however, requires more than good data. It requires physical action.
SPARETECH is moving the market beyond insights and recommendations toward measurable outcomes: lower inventory with the same uptime. To reach the 60% goal, every maintenance professional needs confidence that the right part will be available when needed, even if it sits on another company's shelf. SPARETECH's AI will secure that availability.
"Every part sitting idle is cash that could be working somewhere else. We are building AI that makes sure the right part is available when a plant needs it and put those idle parts back into circulation, so the money tied up on the shelf can go back to growing the business."
Dr. Lukas Biedermann, COO and Co-Founder, SPARETECH
Why now
Industrial automation keeps expanding, and a single new production line can add thousands of spare parts that someone has to stock. The problem grows with every machine that is installed. With the cost of capital rising, manufacturers can no longer afford to keep that much money sitting on the shelf. At the same time, AI can now secure availability at a scale no team could manage by hand.
"Often building resilience in supply chain ends up in building more inventories for spare parts. A much more suitable way would be a system, which secures better resilience with up to 60% less inventories sitting on the shelves. SPARETECH is exactly doing this. A fascinating opportunity especially for the manufacturing industry."
Joe Kaeser, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Siemens Energy and Daimler Truck
"SPARETECH is exactly the kind of business we back. Idle spare parts are a large, overlooked pool of wasted resources, and putting them back to work gives manufacturers a measurable return and the planet less waste. We are delighted to partner with Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."
Michelle Capiod, Co-Founding Partner, Blume Equity
Investing in innovation and expansion
SPARETECH will use the funding to continue building the AI that secures spare part availability for industrial companies and put their surplus parts back into circulation, expand its presence in North America and new regions, and deepen its work with existing customers.
"The next stage of SPARETECH's growth runs through North America. American manufacturers operate large plant networks with a lot of capital tied up in spare parts, and they need a partner built for that scale. Insight has spent decades helping software companies grow in the United States, and we are excited to support Martin, Lukas, and the team as they scale."
Brad Fiedler, Managing Director, Insight Partners
"The digital world is moving into the physical one, and Germany has the industrial substance to lead that shift. SPARETECH is building industrial AI for spare parts management, and it already gives maintenance and procurement teams confidence in uncertain times. This is where industrial AI starts to pay off for global manufacturers."
Christian Miele, General Partner, Headline
Learn more at sparetech.io .

SPARETECH's enterprise AI software empowers global manufacturers to reduce their spare parts spend and inventory. Built on verified original manufacturer data, the platform standardizes material master data, right-sizes inventory across plants, and enables sourcing and surplus resale across the network. Maintenance and procurement teams know what they have, get what they need, and sell what they don't.

By Amit Chowdhry

Primordial Labs: $18 Million Series A Funding To Expand AI-Powered Military Command And Control Platform
Primordial Labs, a defense technology company developing natural-language command and control software for military systems, has raised $18 million in Series A funding to expand deployment of its Anura platform. The investment will support the company’s engineering and product development operations while accelerating adoption across military vehicles, aircraft, and uncrewed systems. The financing was led by Ballistic Ventures, with participation from existing investors Squadra Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures.
Founded in 2021 and headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, Primordial Labs develops technology that allows military personnel to interact with complex equipment using natural-language instructions.
Its Anura platform functions as a software layer between human operators and the systems they control.
Modern military platforms often incorporate multiple sensors, radios, displays, and autonomous systems, each with separate interfaces.
Operating this equipment can create significant demands on personnel, particularly when crews must coordinate different systems during fast-moving missions.
Anura is designed to simplify these interactions by allowing operators to communicate goals and instructions in natural language.
The system translates those instructions into individual tasks and coordinates their execution across connected equipment.
It also monitors the results and adjusts activities as operational conditions change.
The platform is intended to support human-machine teaming by reducing the number of separate interfaces operators must manage.
Primordial Labs has integrated Anura with more than a dozen crewed and uncrewed platforms across land and air applications.
In October 2026, the company announced a master teaming agreement with General Dynamics Land Systems.
The partnership is intended to bring Anura to ground combat vehicles across the General Dynamics Land Systems portfolio, including the Abrams tank.
The company is also delivering licenses for small uncrewed aircraft systems to U.S. Army and special operations units.
These licenses are available through the Army’s UAS Marketplace.
Two Small Business Innovation Research Phase III awards received in 2026 expand the company’s work into Army rotary-wing aircraft and the U.S. Air Force’s MQ-9 ground control station.
These projects provide opportunities to demonstrate the platform in different operating environments.
Anura’s architecture is designed to integrate with existing equipment rather than requiring military customers to redesign entire systems.
The approach aligns with the Modular Open Systems Approach, which emphasizes interoperability and flexibility across defense platforms.
Primordial believes this design can help military organizations adopt the technology across different equipment manufacturers and operational environments.
The company’s founders bring experience developing autonomous and AI-enabled technologies at Lockheed Martin.
Co-Founder and CEO Lee Ritholtz and Co-Founder and CTO Adrian Pope previously worked at Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works.
They participated in the development and deployment of small uncrewed aircraft systems and helped establish the Lockheed Martin Artificial Intelligence Center.
Their experience also included autonomous control technologies and human-machine teaming projects.
Primordial’s workforce combines engineering professionals with former special operations personnel.
The company intends to use the financing to expand its engineering, product, and commercial teams while fulfilling existing defense contracts.
Management also sees potential long-term applications outside the military.
Industries including mining, energy, logistics, and public safety increasingly operate autonomous equipment alongside human workers.
These environments may benefit from interfaces that allow personnel to coordinate complex systems through natural-language instructions.
For now, Primordial is concentrating on military deployments, with the $18 million financing supporting broader implementation of Anura across existing and future platforms.

“Crews on every platform are being asked to employ more capability with fewer people, much faster, and with less time for training. Anura provides humans and machines with a shared understanding of the mission and operating context, making systems easier to field, use, and learn. Lee Ritholtz, Co-Founder And CEO Of Primordial Labs
“The military doesn’t need another proprietary interface for every new system. It needs technology that makes existing and future capabilities work together. EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:45 PM
EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
EagleRock has completed two acquisitions in the Midland Basin for a combined $15.4 million and entered into an agreement with Double Eagle V covering approximately 35,000 additional dedicated acres. The transactions expand EagleRock’s surface land and infrastructure operations in the Permian Basin while increasing its exposure to water management and royalty revenue opportunities.
The additional acreage dedication increases the land dedicated to EagleRock by Double Eagle in the Midland Basin to approximately 105,000 acres.
The new agreement covers approximately 35,000 acres across Midland and Glasscock counties in Texas.
It represents an increase of approximately 50% in Double Eagle’s dedicated acreage within the region.
EagleRock expects the agreement to generate additional royalty revenue without requiring an upfront capital investment.
This structure reflects the company’s capital-light operating model, which uses agreements with energy producers to generate income from the use of surface land and associated infrastructure.
Double Eagle V is an active private operator in the Midland Basin and EagleRock’s largest shareholder.
The additional dedication strengthens the relationship between the two companies and provides EagleRock with exposure to future development activity.
Management expects the agreement to begin making a meaningful revenue contribution in 2027.
Additional growth could follow as Double Eagle advances drilling and completion activities across the dedicated acreage.
Alongside the agreement, EagleRock acquired two properties totaling approximately 2,000 acres.
The acquisitions were completed at an aggregate price of $15.4 million.
EagleRock financed the purchases through cash on hand and borrowings under its existing revolving credit facility.
The company said the assets were purchased at a valuation below 10 times EBITDA.
One property is located directly adjacent to EagleRock’s existing Shallow Valley operations.
The other is adjacent to the newly announced Double Eagle V acreage dedication.
The geographic proximity is intended to support operational coordination and improve the company’s ability to serve customers.
The acquired properties provide additional water supply, storage, and disposal capabilities.
They also include potential opportunities for sand development.
These assets can support oil and gas operators that require water management services and access to infrastructure during drilling and production.
Water handling is a significant operational requirement in the Permian Basin because energy development involves both water consumption and the management of produced water.
Companies providing surface land and related infrastructure can participate in these activities through leases, royalties, and service arrangements.
EagleRock believes the acquisitions will create opportunities to increase revenue while benefiting from shared operating capabilities.
Following the transactions, the company’s Midland Basin portfolio includes approximately 44,000 acres of controlled surface land and approximately 105,000 dedicated acres.
The larger footprint provides additional exposure to energy development across the region.
EagleRock plans to use its existing operations and customer relationships to pursue further opportunities in surface land management and associated infrastructure services.
The acquisitions and acreage agreement reflect its strategy of expanding through complementary properties and capital-efficient commercial arrangements.
KEY QUOTES:
“The Double Eagle V Dedication builds on a relationship that already anchors our Midland Basin position, and it requires no upfront capital from EagleRock. The two acquisitions follow the same approach. They sit next to assets we already have, expand our water supply and storage, and are accretive. Together, these transactions expand our Midland Basin footprint and enhance our ability to serve customers across the region.”
Greg Pipkin, CEO Of EagleRock

The Hadean Energy team
CSIRO spinout Hadean Energy has secured a $15 million grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) to test whether waste heat from heavy industry can cut the cost of making green hydrogen.
ARENA will fund half the $30 million pilot plant proposed for industrial gas supplier BOC’s Western Port site in Victoria. The plant will produce up to 7kg of hydrogen hourly for a neighbouring steelworks. That’s about 85% of the hydrogen needed for annealing, a heat treatment to prevent the steel’s surface from oxidising.
CSIRO and corporate adviser RFC Ambrian launched Hadean in 2023, with the latter’s fund dropping $1.5 million into its seed round that year.
Based at CSIRO’s Clayton research precinct in Melbourne, Hadean is commercialising a tubular solid oxide electrolyser researchers spent eight years developing. Its ceramic tubes use electricity and heat to split steam into hydrogen and oxygen. Hadean estimates that tapping the heat a factory already generates can reduce electricity use by around 30% compared to conventional electrolysers.
In 2024, a prototype ran for 1,000 hours at BlueScope’s Port Kembla steelworks in NSW. It used less than 36 kilowatt-hours of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen by using steam from the plant. The Victorian pilot will scale the system from about one kilowatt to 200-300kW.

Investment to Accelerate iCareManager's Mission to be the System of Record for Intellectual and Developmental Disability and Human Services Providers
iCareManager receives growth investment from Five Elms Capital to build a leading AI-native platform for intellectual and developmental disability (IDD) care providers
Funding will modernize the platform, expand AI capabilities, extend go-to-market reach, and grow the senior leadership team
High-quality customer support remains core to the strategy as iCareManager serves a growing provider base
Five Elms brings deep experience scaling vertical AI-native software businesses
COLUMBIA, Md. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- iCareManager, a leading EHR and care management platform purpose-built for providers supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), today announced a strategic growth investment from Five Elms Capital. The partnership will accelerate product innovation, expand AI capabilities, grow the leadership team, and extend iCareManager's reach to more provider organizations across the U.S.
Continue Reading
iCareManager
IDD providers operate in one of healthcare's most complex environments, navigating state-specific Medicaid waivers, service authorizations, billing, EVV, medication management, and compliance amid workforce shortages and financial pressure. Since 2011, iCareManager has simplified these challenges with technology built specifically for the IDD community.
iCareManager is a unified platform that connects clinical care, service delivery, compliance, workforce management, and billing for human services providers. It brings person-centered planning, eMAR, documentation, scheduling, and Medicaid billing into one view, with built-in support for state-specific rules and EVV. White-glove onboarding and ongoing support help providers adopt it with confidence.
"Over the years, we've built iCareManager with a clear purpose: to make technology work better for the people who provide support and care," said Kamal Sheikh, Co-Founder and CEO of iCareManager. "We're now entering a new era where AI will fundamentally change how people work and interact with technology. The next generation of software won't just help people manage their work; it will increasingly work alongside them. Five Elms understands what we've built, the market we serve, and where we want to go. This partnership gives us the resources and expertise to accelerate that vision, continue innovating, and bring more value to the providers who rely on us every day."
With Five Elms Capital's investment, iCareManager plans to advance the modernization of its technology platform while expanding its next generation of AI-enabled capabilities. "So much of a provider's day runs through iCareManager, from support plans and medication administration to compliance and billing, all on a single record," said Zach Gornet, Vice President at Five Elms Capital. "The AI capabilities the team is building will take real administrative weight off direct support professionals so they can spend more time with the people they serve."
Building on its integrated foundation, iCareManager is developing practical, responsible AI tools that simplify documentation, surface relevant information, and support clinical and operational decisions, reducing administrative work so staff can spend more time on quality care.
"20 years inside the daily work of IDD and assisted living providers has given iCareManager a deep understanding of the data and information behind every service delivered, and that is where AI changes everything," said Babar Nawaz, Co-Founder & COO of iCareManager. "AI will never replace the human. It will replace the admin work and the tedious work, so staff can spend their time helping individuals and residents in a much better way. With Five Elms behind us, this is a game-changing moment for iCareManager. We now have the backing to bring better, safer technology and better AI to every provider out there. The next chapter is going to be very exciting, and we are just getting started."
As iCareManager enters its next phase of growth, its mission is unchanged: giving organizations that support people with intellectual and developmental disabilities technology that simplifies operations, strengthens compliance, and frees caregivers to spend more time with the people they serve.
Austin Gideon, Principal at Five Elms Capital, commented on the investment: "Five Elms backs category-defining software built by exceptional teams, and iCareManager is exactly that. The company has become essential for agencies supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. We're proud to partner with the iCareManager team on the next phase of growth."
Vista Point Advisors acted as the exclusive financial advisor to iCareManager.

CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:46 AM
CIBC Innovation Banking: Growth Financing To Support PortX’s AI-Native Banking Integration Platform
CIBC Innovation Banking has provided growth capital financing to PortX, a Seattle-based financial technology company developing an AI-native integration platform for community banks and credit unions. The financing will support PortX’s product development and expansion as financial institutions seek more efficient ways to connect banking systems, fintech applications, and payment networks.
PortX provides application programming interface infrastructure designed to connect technologies that financial institutions use to manage accounts, process payments, and access customer information.
Its platform currently connects with more than 30 core banking systems and over 100 fintech applications.
It also supports payment connectivity involving the Automated Clearing House network, the Federal Reserve’s FedNow instant payment system, and wire transfers.
These integrations are intended to help community banks and credit unions modernize operations without replacing their existing core systems.
Smaller financial institutions frequently face challenges when adopting new technology because traditional banking platforms may require customized integrations with outside applications.
Developing and maintaining these connections can require substantial engineering resources, create additional operating expenses, and delay the introduction of new financial products.
PortX aims to address these issues through reusable infrastructure that connects multiple systems through a common integration framework.
The platform is designed to support real-time information exchange, application interoperability, and consistent data access.
PortX has also incorporated governance capabilities intended to support the adoption of AI within regulated financial institutions.
Its infrastructure allows activities to be logged, traced, and tracked, supporting oversight of automated processes and interactions across connected systems.
The company holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications, reflecting its investment in information security controls and management practices.
PortX believes these capabilities are increasingly important as banks and credit unions introduce AI tools into operations involving sensitive financial information.
The company reports that Sound Credit Union has reclaimed more than 10,000 business hours through its implementation of PortX technology.
This example highlights the potential for integrated banking infrastructure to reduce repetitive work and improve productivity.
PortX intends to use CIBC’s financing to support continued growth and develop additional platform capabilities.
The financing provides nondilutive capital, allowing the company to expand without issuing additional equity as part of the transaction.
PortX is backed by investors including Fuse, BankTech Ventures, Curql Collective, the American Bankers Association, EJF Capital, and Allied Solutions.
Its investor relationships represent participation from more than 350 financial institutions.
CIBC Innovation Banking provides financing to growth-stage technology and life sciences companies across North America.
The organization has more than $11 billion in funds managed and has supported more than 700 venture capital- and private equity-backed companies over the past six and a half years.
The investment supports PortX’s efforts to expand access to modern financial infrastructure among community banks and credit unions seeking to improve efficiency and introduce additional digital services.
KEY QUOTES:
“Community banks and credit unions have deep relationships with their customers and understand their markets uniquely well. PortX enables them to move faster and more efficiently by connecting their core systems, applications, and payment rails through a modern, API-first platform. Our customers are already seeing significant benefits, Sound Credit Union is one example of more than 10,000 business hours reclaimed. With CIBC Innovation Banking’s support, we’re accelerating our ability to help more institutions unlock similar efficiencies.”
David Wexler, CEO Of PortX
“CIBC Innovation Banking is delighted to support PortX’s growth initiatives with a substantive amount of non-dilutive capital. PortX provides community banks and credit unions with access to core and application banking platform solutions that would otherwise be costly and time consuming to build on their own. We’re excited to be alongside them in their growth journey.”
John Flemming, Managing Director Of CIBC Innovation Banking

By Amit Chowdhry

Ring Launches With $249.99 Drone Cam And $999.99 Rover Cam For Autonomous Security
Ring, Amazon’s smart home security company, has announced Ring Robotics, a new category of autonomous security devices designed to patrol, investigate disturbances, and respond to potential threats across homes and businesses. The launch includes two products: Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor security camera priced at $249.99, and Ring Rover Cam, a mobile security robot for businesses priced at $999.99.
The new product category expands Ring’s traditional security offerings, which have primarily relied on stationary cameras, video doorbells, motion sensors, and alarm systems.
Ring Robotics introduces mobile devices that can autonomously navigate indoor environments, investigate security alerts, and provide video coverage in areas that fixed cameras may not reach.
Both products are powered by AI Pilot, a proprietary navigation and intelligence system that combines cameras, computer vision models, on-device sensors, and cloud processing.
AI Pilot allows the devices to map indoor spaces, identify important locations, and navigate between designated patrol points.
During setup, users can carry Ring Drone Cam through their homes or allow Ring Rover Cam to explore a business environment autonomously.
The system analyzes the environment and generates a floor plan, automatically identifying rooms and suggesting locations that may require additional security attention.
These locations can include entrances, windows, cash registers, storage areas, and corridors.
Customers can customize patrol points and establish routes based on their security preferences.
Once a patrol begins, AI Pilot calculates a route to the selected destination while navigating around furniture, shelving, and other obstacles.
The technology is designed to reduce the manual effort associated with monitoring multiple areas of a property.
Ring Drone Cam For Residential Security
Ring Drone Cam is a flying indoor camera designed to provide security coverage throughout a home without requiring a stationary camera in every room.
The device remains docked when not in use and can be activated manually, through scheduled flights, or in response to compatible Ring security alerts.
Customers can establish custom flight routes and designate areas for the drone to inspect.
When a connected Ring camera, sensor, or alarm detects activity, Ring Drone Cam can automatically travel to previously configured patrol points.
The device provides 2K video resolution, a 148-degree field of view, and the ability to rotate 360 degrees.
Two integrated LED lights automatically activate in low-light conditions to improve visibility.
The camera integrates with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms.
Customers can also control the device through the new Alexa Home Map interface.
Ring envisions applications such as checking whether windows are closed before leaving home or investigating an unexpected security notification while traveling.
By allowing a single camera to move between rooms, Ring Drone Cam provides an alternative to installing multiple fixed indoor cameras.
The company plans to begin shipping Ring Drone Cam in the United States on January 27, 2027, at a retail price of $249.99.
The device remains subject to required Federal Communications Commission authorization before it can be offered for sale.
Ring Rover Cam For Business Security
Ring Rover Cam is a purpose-built autonomous security robot designed for commercial environments.
The product was developed partly in response to feedback from Amazon Astro customers who identified mobile security as one of the robot’s most useful capabilities.
Ring incorporated lessons from Astro while developing a device focused specifically on business security applications.
Ring Rover Cam can patrol commercial spaces, investigate disturbances, and provide video coverage throughout a property.
Business owners can send the robot to designated rooms or patrol locations through the Ring app.
Upon reaching a destination, the device performs a 360-degree scan.
Customers can also schedule recurring patrols during periods such as after closing or before opening.
When a connected Ring security device is triggered, Rover can autonomously travel to programmed locations to investigate.
The robot features an adjustable periscope camera that can extend above counters, shelving, and other obstacles.
Customers can configure the camera height for individual patrol points and save those settings for subsequent visits.
The device also includes a siren, a visible light tower, and two-way audio capabilities.
These features are designed to provide active deterrence while allowing business operators to communicate remotely.
Ring Rover Cam supports streaming and recording in up to 4K video while moving or patrolling.
Unlike security systems that record only at fixed monitoring points, Rover can capture footage continuously along its route.
The robot also supports continuous person-motion detection, including while docked.
Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping to U.S. customers on December 16, 2026, priced at $999.99.
AI Integration And Privacy Features
Both Ring Robotics devices integrate with Ring’s existing security ecosystem, providing customers with a centralized interface for managing cameras, alarms, and autonomous patrols.
The products also include privacy controls designed to indicate when recording is occurring.
Ring Drone Cam powers down while docked, with its camera disabled until a flight is activated.
Ring Rover Cam includes a Sleep Mode that retracts its periscope and disables its microphone.
Both devices feature visible recording indicators, while Rover also provides recording information through its onboard screen.
